transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-25
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Leah Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Aria Gomez (Head of ML, OceanGuard), Connor Lee (Platform Eng Lead), Priya Nair (Security Architect), Nate Rivers (Product)
Shared artifacts: QBR deck (drive.google.com/ocg-qbr), cost-sample CSV (s3://redwood/qbr/oceanguard/90d.csv)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Quick roll call, and then we'll walk through the 90-day usage, cost, incidents and a proposed spike.
[00:21] Aria: Yep, thanks Maya. We had a couple of folks in flight so Connor's on. Priya will jump into security parts later.
[00:30] Maya: Great. Leah's going to surface the adoption numbers, Jordan will cover reliability root cause and recommended optimizations.
[00:45] Leah: Ok, quick bullets - overall tokens up ~38% month-over-month, active endpoints increased 22%, but latency sensitive routes (search/autocomplete) are driving majority of spend because of small prompt & high qps.
[01:10] Connor: To add, we saw two spikes in late August where p95 increased and we had a failover to the fallback model which bumped cost x2 for those hours.
[01:30] Jordan: Right - that fallover was because the autoscaler timing + a model load pause when the dedup cache missed and then the runtime retried - basically a cold-start-ish scenario combined with KV cache thrash. Our logs show lots of small requests with no prefix cache hits so KV caches weren't reused.
[02:00] Aria: When you say KV cache thrash, are we talking about dedicated per-tenant pools or the shared hosted pool?
[02:12] Jordan: Shared hosted pool in this instance, which means eviction policy was more aggressive. With Dedicated, you can pin hot models and the K V cache persistence is more durable. But that comes at committed cost.
[02:35] Aria: Yeah, that's the tradeoff. We want to avoid the x2 billing blips during peak.
[02:45] Maya: Understood. On the cost side we've run the token-level breakdown — Connor, we uploaded your CSV and did a route-by-route analysis. In the deck slide 6 we show that three endpoints represent 68% of token spend but only 12% of total requests.
[03:10] Connor: That's exactly what we saw in our analytics too. The small prompts for autocomplete are cheap per request but super expensive per-token because of high repetition.
[03:25] Leah: So recommended levers: prefix caching (we call it prefix / KV caching), request-side batching for similar latency windows, and quantization profiles for the models used by those routes. We also highlighted TTL tuning on cache and retry/backoff tuning to reduce cold-loads.
[03:55] Priya: Quick security interjection — for Dedicated we need to verify BYOK KMS path, HSM support, and audit log retention. We also need SSO integration with our IdP and RBAC roles for the ops team.
[04:15] Maya: Absolutely, we have a SOC2 pack and a KMS integration diagram. We'll share the architecture diagram you asked for. Note that on Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS + HSM via standard KM S APIs and we can produce audit logs at token route granularity.
[04:46] Priya: I heard KM S — sorry transcription — yes, please send the HSM notes. Also, network segmentation details, we have a strict DMZ rule.
[05:00] Jordan: For the reliability incident root cause — we replayed the trace and saw the autoscaler window was 12s with concurrent model loads; when the concurrency hit those small routes the model load queue hit the hard limit and a fallback policy routed to a smaller variant which is functionally fine but triggered a different tokenization path and higher usage.
[05:30] Aria: So the immediate mitigation is reduce autoscaler cooldown and adjust model load concurrency?
[05:38] Jordan: Yes, plus enabling prefix caching on the route and reusing a warmed Dedicated pool for the busiest endpoints. That avoids the model load thrash.
[05:52] Maya: Cost-wise, if we apply batching with a 50–80ms batching window and prefix caching, our model shows a 25-30% reduction on those high-spend routes. Quantizing the model to 4-bit where acceptable for latency can shave another 15% with minor quality delta.
[06:20] Connor: 50–80ms window for batching — our product team says 50ms is the upper bound for UX. Any longer and our Typeahead will feel laggy.
[06:35] Jordan: Understood. The point estimate we used for savings assumed batching at 40ms and prefix caching; we can re-run with a 30-50ms window. Also one approach is adaptive batching so latency-sensitive routes get smaller windows and lower-cost background routes get longer windows.
[07:00] Nate: Are adaptive batching configs something Redwood exposes in the console?
[07:06] Maya: Yes, in Redwood Console you can set per-route batching windows, split by model variant and priority. We'll demo that in the spike.
[07:20] Priya: On compliance, audit retention: we need 3 years of immutable logs, and encryption at rest with customer-managed keys. Is that supported right now?
[07:36] Maya: For Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed KMS, and you can configure log forwarding to your SIEM. Immutable retention for 3 yrs will require the log archiving addon — we'll put that in the security pack.
[07:55] Aria: Back to next steps on cost: can you show the delta between Hosted optimization vs Dedicated with reserved capacity? We want an apples-to-apples monthly run rate to feed Finance.
[08:12] Leah: Yes, and we'll include amortized reserved capacity pricing with burst costs in the one-pager.
[08:25] Maya: We'll share a 90-day run-rate and a proposed 3-month Dedicated pilot cost.
[08:35] Connor: For the pilot we need to validate model-level latency p95, and the cold start rate. If those look good, we'll talk contract.
[08:46] Jordan: For the pilot we'll instrument synthetic traffic close to your production token distribution, and run a 72-hour spike with controlled QPS ramps. We'll collect p50/p95/p99, cold-start events, and KV cache hit ratios.
[09:05] Aria: Sounds good. A couple of specific asks: 1) can you include per-token unit economics for embedding vs generation? 2) how does cost behave when we enable quantization per model?
[09:20] Jordan: Yes to both — embeddings are a different unit but we have per-embed unit cost breakdown. For quantization we will run an inference-quality sweep and show how token costs change per quant profile. We'll include a small quality delta estimate.
[09:40] Maya: Also to flag for Connor and Aria — we saw one config drift where the retry policy was too aggressive which amplified replays during the incident; we'll recommend retry hardening in the runbook.
[10:00] Connor: Good to call that out. On rollout: if the spike looks good, what is estimated lead time to move 3 routes to Dedicated?
[10:10] Maya: From pilot success to dedicated rollout with reservations, typical timeline 3–6 weeks (access, network setup with your VPC, KMS integration, and capacity provisioning). If you want faster, we can do a hybrid where we pin a warm Dedicated pool and keep overflow on Hosted for 2 weeks.
[10:30] Priya: For VPC peering and private endpoints we'll need the network diagram and a contact. I'll share that after the call.
[10:40] Aria: Anything on fallback policies? We need graceful degradation that doesn't double cost when a failover happens.
[10:48] Jordan: Recommend a model-variant-based fallback that preserves tokenization path. For example, fallback to a same-tokenizer smaller variant rather than a different family. Redwood supports variant families and automatic fallback routing.
[11:10] Nate: Any quick wins we can apply now without Dedicated?
[11:18] Leah: Tune retry/backoff, set shorter autoscaler cooldowns, enable prefix caching on those three routes, and adjust batching windows — these are low-risk and can be toggled in console.
[11:36] Aria: Ok let's do that first then run the spike.
[11:42] Maya: Action summary — Maya will send the 90-day cost delta + one-pager; Jordan runs quant/kv sims; Leah books spike; Priya will confirm KMS requirements; Connor shares three route distributions.
[12:10] Connor: I'll add the route CSV to the shared folder by tomorrow.
[12:18] Priya: I'll open a ticket for the KMS owners and attach the certificate chain.
[12:24] Maya: Great. Any other questions?
[12:30] Aria: One more — are there any known vendor features to reduce tokenization overhead for small prompt patterns?
[12:40] Jordan: There's work in Redwood Optimize (we sometimes call it Redwood Opt in notes) on request-level token bucketing and de-duplication; we'll include current roadmap items in the doc. Not GA but it's in beta with a few customers.
[13:05] Maya: Alright thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the deck, cost CSV, security pack and scheduling links.
[13:15] Meeting ends.

Notes on transcription: Some technical terms munged (e.g., KM S for KMS, K V cache spacing). Natural speech patterns, short interruptions, and occasional misattributed speaker lines are present.
